headline: Brazil ADRs crash 20–50% after Lula's surprise re-election (EWZ −28%) while US futures edge higher; EQT agrees to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal ahead of a week with the FOMC and Microsoft/Alphabet/Amazon earnings.
notes: Scheduled run ~7:49 a.m. CT, before the 8:30 a.m. CT open: PRE-MARKET. All movers use live pre-market data dated Oct 26 (Yahoo and StockAnalysis via the Mac browser); StockAnalysis movers pages checked as dated Oct 26, 2026.

Quality movers screened from Yahoo's US list of stocks ≥$5 and ≥$2B (top 3,000 by market cap; 831 had an Oct 26 pre-market quote ≥$5), plus StoneCo, PagSeguro and Surgery Partners added from StockAnalysis's movers pages. Pre-market price ≥$5 used for the $5 filter, so BBD, SBS, INTR, ABEV, BSBR (all below $5 pre-market) appear in the under-$5 tables instead. Names with <10K pre-market shares left out.
PBR.A (−22.4%, 1.88M sh) left out of the losers table as a duplicate share class of PBR; MELI added instead. ELPC (−20.1%) left out on 9K shares.

Brazil sell-off dominates the losers list: Lula won a fourth term (≈51.8%–48.2%) over Flávio Bolsonaro, a surprise; Bolsonaro says he will seek to annul the result. Non-Brazil losers below the top 10: FICO (−9.6% on 7K sh; Wells Fargo downgrade), MRNA (−7.0%), EQT (−6.4%).

Gap watchlist applied strictly. Passing: SGRY, RRC, MRNA, EQT. Brazil ADRs gapped far more but the catalyst (an election) is not one of the listed catalyst types, so they are excluded (same treatment as last week's macro/competition moves). XNCR (+34%, ESMO kidney-cancer data) fails the $2B market-cap test ($1.87B).
SGRY catalyst is an FT report of late-stage take-private talks (~$20/share, ~$6B incl. debt); Investing.com describes it as an agreement — treat as reported, not confirmed by the company.

MRNA: Investing.com attributes the drop to Phase 3 melanoma data for intismeran (42% risk reduction vs 49% in Phase 2b); ZeroHedge says pancreatic-cancer vaccine results. Investing.com's specific version used.

META: ZeroHedge (8:15 a.m. ET) had META +2.4% on a $95B equity-raise plan, but live quotes at ~8:50 a.m. ET show −0.6% to −0.7% (Yahoo/StockAnalysis) on very heavy volume ($1.37B traded). Live quotes used.
AXG excluded: StockAnalysis shows −99.5% vs a $10.84 prior close while Yahoo's prior close is $0.054 (−7.8%) — reverse-split/price artifact.
Nasdaq-100 Friday cash close from Yahoo (^NDX 28,957.53, ≈0.0%) is consistent with QQQ's −0.01% close.
Relative volume = pre-market volume ÷ 3-month average full-day volume (Yahoo), so values are naturally small before the open.
Leveraged ETF volume is pre-market volume vs the 3-month average daily volume (Yahoo) because a 30-day average was not retrieved. FANG+ index has no pre-market quote (null).
Under-$5 lists come from StockAnalysis's top-20 pre-market pages plus Brazil names checked directly; float n/a (Yahoo shares outstanding used where noted).
Unusual options activity: no options-flow source available.
After-close earnings list from ZeroHedge's calendar and Yahoo; NUE and PSA named by Yahoo as reporting today (timing not confirmed).
No git commands were run; the Mac publish agent handles commit and push.
drivers: US futures are modestly higher (S&P 500 +0.3%, Nasdaq-100 +0.5%) after Friday's second straight weekly loss, helped by chips (SOXX +1.6%, MU +2.7%) and a 2% drop in oil (WTI ~$101) as Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials meet Iran in Tehran and Iran floats a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; Trump says it is 'decision time' on a deal or strikes. The big shock is Brazil: Lula won a fourth term in a surprise runoff result, and Brazilian ADRs are collapsing — EWZ −28%, XP −51%, StoneCo −39%, Itaú −28%, Nubank −26%, Petrobras −22%, MercadoLibre −15% — with Santander −4% on its Brazil exposure. In deals, EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal (0.987 EQT per RRC share, >$50B combined EV): RRC +11.5%, EQT −6.4%; an FT report says Bon Secours Mercy is near a ~$20/share take-private of Surgery Partners (+24%). Neoclouds are weak (CoreWeave −3.4%, IREN −2.4%) after Musk said debt markets have almost shut off funding for companies without revenue outside AI data centers; Meta is trading heavily around flat after announcing plans to raise up to $95B in equity for AI spending. The week is packed: FOMC decision Wednesday (hold expected under Chair Warsh, December hike largely priced), Microsoft and Alphabet Wednesday, Amazon, Q3 GDP and September PCE Thursday; the 10-year yield is near 4.99% and the VIX near 19.
